messages:
maia-arch: quick RFC follow-up: how do we safely let a region accept requests when its canonical residency is elsewhere? need operator-safe pattern for short bursts without breaking residency contracts.

oliver-sre: two obvious options: 1) simple redirect to canonical (safe but high latency), 2) accept locally and mark as shadow-write (low latency, higher complexity).

maia-arch: leaning shadow-write for UX. plan: local ack, write with `shadow` flag, async reconcile to canonical. must surface staleness window.

dean-eng: engineering cost: need lease guard to avoid split-primary writes. propose temporary lease token with TTL and automatic swapback when reconcile complete.

anya-ml: model outputs sensitive to stale context. add `x-response-staleness-ms` header and flag low-confidence outputs. Optimize should get alerts when staleness > threshold.

sara-eng: API change: `X-Redwood-Residency: strict|flex` header for tenant preference. default strict. Console toggle for enterprise override.

oliver-sre: telemetry list: `shadow_write_rate`, `reconciliation_lag_p95`, `shadow_conflict_count`. need runbook: force strict header at proxy to roll back quickly.

ops-bot: scheduled sim job #721 created (2x qps, 3m sustain). results -> https://ci.internal/sim/721

maia-arch: next steps: I'll write short RFC appendix with policy YAML, header spec, metrics, and rollout checklist. please review when I post.
